A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LAZYREVIEW and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing material can be matched across relocation and renumbering, including the appendix figures preceding v2's new analysis.

before.justification: v1 reports original annotation-agreement measurements, LLM classification experiments, evaluator validation, and a controlled human review-rewriting study.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a class-level analysis of Qwen predictions on Round 3 annotations.

M1.justification: The GPT-4 segment-extraction pipeline, iterative annotation, prompting and exemplar-selection methods, LoRA instruction tuning, and Qwen silver-label generation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ARR-2022 reviews from NLPEER, classification and review-rewriting tasks, and TULU/SCIRIFF training mixtures. Appendix A.15 analyzes existing Round 3 coverage; the proposed application to distinguishing human and AI reviews is not evaluated.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same random/majority baselines, seven LLM configurations, exemplar-selection comparators, and review-rewriting control conditions. Changes to model-report citations do not introduce different models.

E3.justification: Reported splits, model sizes, metrics, prompting conditions, data mixtures, training settings, and human-study procedures are unchanged. The new confusion-matrix analysis uses retained Round 3 annotation data without reporting a changed evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: v2 adds Appendix A.15 and Figure 16 to examine which categories challenge Qwen and relate its errors to human annotation disagreements. This is one targeted error analysis; existing exemplar-selection, data-mixture, evaluator-alignment, and silver-annotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Cross-validation reporting, agreement statistics, confidence plots, and numerical uncertainty displays are retained. No new run counts, seeds, intervals, or statistical estimation procedures are reported. Calling agreement 'moderate' instead of 'substantial' changes interpretation rather than estimation.

E6.justification: Figure 16 newly reports Qwen's class-level confusion counts, with Appendix A.15 identifying difficulties with 'Contradict expectations' and 'Negative results'. Existing numerical results in Tables 2–5 and 10–15, including model scores and review-rewriting preferences, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definitions and mathematical descriptions are unchanged. Neither version introduces new theoretical propositions, proofs, derivations, or formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about the dataset, improved annotation guidelines, benefits of examples and instruction tuning, and improved review quality from lazy-thinking feedback.

C2.justification: Section 2.2 replaces the belief that lazy thinking appears only in weaknesses with a rationale for restricting collection to that section. Section 2.4 describes agreement above 0.4 as 'moderate' rather than 'substantial'. Appendix A.15 links model errors to human disagreements, and Limitations introduces a hypothesis about distinguishing human-written and AI-generated reviews.

D1.justification: The page-one code-access link changes from UKPLab/arxiv2025-lazy-review to UKPLab/acl2025-lazy-review. Model identifiers, prompt templates, LoRA hyperparameters, hardware, computational budgets, and licensing disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work coverage and novelty positioning are retained. Changes such as OpenAI to Achiam, Team to Mesnard, and AI to Young identify the same model reports; other reference revisions update titles, years, author lists, or publication venues for matched works.

P1.justification: There are limited paragraph revisions concerning collection rationale, agreement interpretation, and limitations, plus heading, bibliography, and acknowledgement edits. The main narrative and section order remain intact, with one short appendix subsection added.

P2.justification: v2 adds confusion-matrix Figure 16, renumbers the former Figures 16–18 as 17–19, and moves Figure 2 from page 4 to page 5. Table 4's caption now explains its existing red/gray highlighting. Existing graphical content is retained, with localized layout and bibliography reflow.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.15 and Figure 16 make Qwen's category-specific failures inspectable, adding useful diagnostic evidence beyond v1's aggregate scores. The revised collection rationale and more restrained agreement interpretation also improve clarity. These are limited gains: the main experimental evidence is unchanged, and the suggested human/AI review-discrimination application remains untested.
